sentences.text:
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Tirumala Devi Eada
 Appeal Suit No.3220 Of 2004
Judgment:

(per Hon'ble Smt. Justice Tirumala Devi Eada) This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short 'the Act') is preferred by the Special Deputy Collector, LA Unit,
South Central Railway New Broad Gauge Line, Karimangar, aggrieved by the order and decree dated 30.12.2003 passed in O.P.No.91 of 1997 by the learned Senior Civil Judge at Peddapalli (hereinafter referred to as 'the reference Court').
2.
For convenience and clarity, the parties herein are referred to as they were arrayed before the reference Court.

3. The facts of the case in brief are that on a requisition made by the Special Deputy Collector, LA Unit, South Central Railway, the lands to an extent of Ac.8-9 guntas and 100 Sq.Yards, situated at Cheekurai Village of Peddapalli Mandal, were acquired for the purpose of formation of Broad Guage Railway Line.

A draft notification under Section 4(1) of the Act was published in the Gazette No.12,
on 25.04.1995.

After following due procedure, the Land Acquisition Officer has passed an award on 08.04.1996 granting Rs.16,000/- per acre to category No.I lands, Rs.15,000/-
AKS,J & ETD,J AS No.3220_2004 per acre to category No.II lands, Rs.12,000/- per acre for category No.III lands and also awarded Rs.26,649/- to three wells.
He also granted Rs.100/- to each tappable toddy tree and Rs.160/- to two tappable Sendhi trees, towards compensation.
Aggrieved by the said award, the claimants have made an application for reference and the same was referred under Section 18 of the Act to the reference Court.

4. The reference Court has framed the following points for consideration:
"1. Whether the award No.4, dt.8.4.1996 passed by the Land Acquisition Officer is not reasonable and adequate?
2. Whether the claimants are entitled to get enhanced compensation to the acquired lands, wells and trees, if so, at what rate?"

sentences.text: To prove their case, the claimants got examined PWs 1 to 8 and got marked Exs.A1 to A7.
One D.Venkatesham, Special Deputy Tahsildar in South Central Railway's, Special Deputy Collector's Officer at Karimnagar got examined as RW1 and Ex.B1 was marked.

6. Based on the evidence on record, the reference Court has ordered the compensation @
Rs.40,000/- per acre for all the acquired lands, for the wells by one time over and above the AKS,J & ETD,J AS No.3220_2004 compensation granted by the Land Acquisition Officer, for the toddy tree @ Rs.200/- and for the Sendhi tree Rs.150/- each, apart from awarding statutory benefits.
Aggrieved by the said order and decree passed by the reference Court, the Special Deputy Collector has preferred the present appeal.

7. Heard the submissions of Smt.T.Suhasini, learned Standing Counsel for the appellant, Sri A.Sudarshan Reddy, learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 to 7 and 18 to 21 and 24, Sri G.Madhusudan Reddy, learned counsel for respondent Nos.25 and 26.

8 . Learned appellant counsel has submitted that the Reference Court has erroneously enhanced the compensation to Rs.40,000/- per acre for all the acquired lands and for the wells by one time over and above the compensation granted by the Land Acquisition Officer, and that it is without any basis.

He further argued that the claimants have not filed any documentary proof to show the nature of crops and the income earned by them on the acquired lands and that the reference Court should not have relied upon Exs.A1 & A2, the sale deeds which are not comparable to the value of the land acquired and that the entire lands do not fall under one category while the reference Court has enhanced the compensation by treating them under one category.
He therefore, prayed to set AKS,J & ETD,J AS No.3220_2004 aside the order and decree of the Reference Court by allowing this appeal.
9. The learned respondent counsel has prayed to uphold the order and decree passed by the reference Court stating that it is a well reasoned order.

10. Based on the above rival contentions, this Court frames the following points for determination:
1. Whether the claimants are not entitled for enhancement of compensation?
2. Whether the order and decree of the reference Court need any interference?

3. To what relief?
11. POINT NO.1:
a) A perusal of Ex.B1/the award passed by Land Acquisition Officer, reveals that the sale transaction at Sl.No.13 dated 30.12.1994 pertains to dry land in survey No.22 and it was sold @30,000/- per acre in the same village and there are some other sale transactions shown in Kothapalli village of Peddapalli Mandal, wherein the dry land was shown to have been sold @ Rs50,700/-

2 per acre at Sl.No.22 dated 07.12.1992 in survey No.398 and 406.

sentences.text:
The Land Acquisition Officer has not considered the sales at Sl.No.13 because a meager extent is sold under the said sale AKS,J &
ETD,J AS No.3220_2004 transactions i.e. to an extent of Ac.0-04 guntas and that he has not considered the sale transaction at Sl.No.14 because of the strategic position of the said land, which is near Vaagu and are fertile with red chelka lands and that there is no similarity by geographical position between the lands under acquisition and the said lands.

The Land Acquisition Officer has observed that the lands shown at Sl.No.22 are dry lands of Kothapalli village and that Kothapalli transactions are obtained for fixing-up the land value for wet lands of Cheekurai Village, since there were no wet land sales at Cheekurai village and the dry lands sale of Kothapalli shown at Sl.No.22 is discarded as the dry lands sale statistics of Cheekurai village are available.
b) A perusal of the evidence of PWs 1 to 3 reveals that PW1 is the husband of one P.Sujatha who is one of the vendors in the sale transaction shown under Exs.A1 and A2.
A perusal of Ex.A1 reveal that the land to an extent of Ac.0.13 guntas was sold in survey Nos.605, 606/e, 583, 631, 632/e, 602, 603 and 604 @ Rs.22,500/-.
A perusal of Ex.A2 reveals that the land to an extent of Ac.0-15 guntas was sold in survey No.398 and 406/a @ Rs.10,000/- per acre and that they were paid Rs.3,800/- for 0.15 guntas.

AKS,J & ETD,J AS No.3220_2004 c) PW1 deposed that the acquired lands are situated adjacent to the lands which were sold under Exs.A1 and A2 and that Kothapalli and Cheekurai villages are situated adjacent to each other and that the acquired lands are similar in all aspects to the lands under Exs.A1 and A2.

d) PW2 is the claimant No.19 in the present case, his evidence reveals that their lands are under SRSP irrigation and that they are wet lands and they used to raise paddy and that all the acquired lands belong to one category.

He further deposed that the land that was acquired would fetch Rs.1,60,000/- per acre and that cheekurai village is merged in Peddapalli township, that a social welfare hostel is situated in their village, and that the acquired lands are suitable for house sites.
e) PW3 is a resident of Karimnagar and is an architectural engineer, whose evidence reveals that he submitted a report by estimating the value of the wells.

f) An overall perusal of the oral and documentary evidence that was placed before the reference Court reveals that Cheekurai and Kothapalli villages are adjacent to each other and even the Land Acquisition Officer has relied upon the sale transactions of Kothapalli for fixing the compensation with regard to the dry lands, AKS,J & ETD,J AS No.3220_2004 which proves the fact that Kothapalli is an adjacent village to Chekurai.

The sale transactions reflected at Sl.Nos.13, 14 and 22 which are shown to be highest are not considered by the Land Acquisition Officer for the reasons as discussed supra.
g) On examining the sale statistics in Ex.B1 and also the sale deeds that are filed under Exs.A1 and A2 it is held that the lands that were acquired, fetch more value than what is awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer.

Therefore, it is held that the claimants are entitled to enhancement of The Special Deputy Collector, vs Egolam Chandraiah on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48534673/
3 compensation and that the enhanced compensation of Rs.40,000/- per acre that is awarded by the reference Court is justified.

sentences.text: Point No.1 is answered accordingly.
12. POINT NO.2:
In view of the reasoned finding arrived at Point No.1, this Court holds that the order and decree of the reference Court do not need any interference.
13. POINT NO.3:
In the result, the appeal is dismissed upholding the order and decree dated 30.12.2003 passed in O.P.No.91 of 1997 by the learned Senior Civil Judge at Peddapalli.
No costs.
AKS,J & ETD,J AS No.3220_2004 Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
ABHINAND KUMAR SHAVILI, J ___________________________ TIRUMALA DEVI EADA, J Date: 6.03.2025 ns
